findings: JWT_SECRET vs JWT_SECRET_KEY name mismatch — Both scripts and cicd.md export JWT_SECRET, but .env.example (the authoritative variable list) defines JWT_SECRET_KEY. If the FastAPI app reads JWT_SECRET_KEY, local pytest runs will silently lack a JWT secret. Align the variable name across both scripts, cicd.md, and verify against the actual app configuration.

Local pytest missing --cov-fail-under=90 — CI runs pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=90; the local gate runs pytest tests/ -m 'not db' with no coverage flag. A developer can reduce coverage below 90% and push successfully. Add either --cov=app --cov-fail-under=90 to the local invocation, or add this divergence explicitly to the Known Limitations section and to the inline comment in both scripts.

PowerShell Invoke-External one-element array splicing — $Arguments[1..($Arguments.Length-1)] with $Arguments.Length -eq 1 evaluates to @(1, 0) rather than an empty array. Fix: $rest = if ($Arguments.Length -gt 1) { $Arguments[1..($Arguments.Length-1)] } else { @() } then & $Arguments[0] @rest.

pre-push hook missing existence check for PS1 on Windows path — The Unix branch guards with 'if [ ! -f $SH_PATH ]'; the Windows branch calls exec powershell.exe unconditionally. If check-before-push.ps1 is absent, the push is blocked but the error is a raw PowerShell complaint. Add a symmetric file-existence check before the exec on the Windows path.
